annotation.title_clean: General Understanding on AI and Copyright in Japan (Overview)
annotation.title_en: General Understanding on AI and Copyright in Japan (Overview)
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Copyright Division, Agency for Cultural Affairs, Japan (Legal Subcommittee, Copyright Subdivision, Cultural Council)
annotation.summary_en: Overview slides of the Japanese Agency for Cultural Affairs' non-binding General Understanding on how the existing Copyright Act applies to generative AI: training-stage exploitation under Article 30-4, infringement at the generation stage, liability of AI businesses, and copyrightability of AI-generated material.
key_provisions_or_claims: Article 30-4 generally permits copyrighted works to be used for AI training for non-enjoyment purposes without permission.
Article 30-4 does not apply where an enjoyment purpose coexists, such as fine-tuning to reproduce specific works, or where it unreasonably prejudices rights holders.
Infringement by AI outputs is judged by the usual similarity and dependence criteria.
AI developers and providers may be liable, depending on measures taken to prevent infringing outputs.
Purely AI-generated material is not copyrightable, but AI used as a tool with human creative contribution can be, and only natural or legal persons can be authors.
